ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in triangle $ABC$, $AD \perp BC$, $CE \perp AB$, with the perpendicular feet being D and E respectively. $AD$ and $CE$ intersect at point H. Given that $EH = EB = 5$ and $CH = 2$, then what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: $EH=EB=5$, $CH=2$,\\
Therefore $EC=EH+CH=7$,\\
Since $AD\perp BC$, $CE\perp AB$,\\
Thus $\angle ADB=\angle AEH=90^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle AHE=\angle CHD$,\\
Thus $\angle BAD=\angle BCE$,\\
In $\triangle HEA$ and $\triangle BEC$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle EAH=\angle BCE \\ \angle AEH=\angle BEC=90^\circ \\ EH=EB\end{array}\right.$,\\
Therefore $\triangle HEA\cong \triangle BEC\left(AAS\right)$,\\
Hence $AE=EC=\boxed{7}$.
